Inference: the evidence strongly fits the outer15s timeout while the first decode was still running. It does NOT prove the exception class or why decode took that long: old logging omitted class/traceback, and no late successful decode was observed. CAM++ embeddings/matches are present independently; telemetry DNS rejection is a background-thread event and is not attributed as the request cause.

Change: server ASR_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=90; backend HTTP connect5s/read100s. Both fit below the existing120s no-progress barrier without changing its deadline, request budget, model/KV/GPU settings or controller. No inference retry/warmup/manual audio was added. HTTP failures remain terminal; an HTTP400 does not become a transport retry. Server notes that cancelling wait_for cannot stop an already running executor thread; existing failed-session cleanup remains responsible for stopping the service generation.

New diagnostics: outer request error contains exception class, decode_audio/executor_inference_wait/response stage, elapsed seconds,90s deadline, session/final identity, nonempty message and executor_may_still_be_running. logger.exception emits traceback. run_inference internal failures also emit class/stage/elapsed/traceback. Client preserves up to4096 response-body characters in its HTTPError and logs class/http stage/elapsed/status/session. Actual exceptions propagate, never swallowed.

Optional noise removal approved in scope: XTServices exports VLLM_NO_USAGE_STATS=1 and DO_NOT_TRACK=1 to the owned services. Installed vLLM usage/usage_lib.py:58-68 and envs.py:637-644 recognize these variables. Existing offline audit remains unchanged; no external connection is permitted.
